Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Exploring Skyline Nexus + Redwood: co-sell mapping & integration

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the product demo last week — our engineering team is optimistic about the integration surface between Skyline Nexus and Redwood's serving runtime. We ran a quick pilot with two joint customers and saw a clear reduction in inference latency for their multi-tenant workloads.

We'd like to move to a formal co-sell/mapping phase and need help from Redwood to:
- identify account overlap between Skyline's installed base and Redwood's target lists
- propose a stewardship/routing model so we avoid duplicate outreach
- define a minimal mutual action plan (MAP) for a joint GTM pilot (30–60 days)

Attached is a slice of our book-of-business for Q3 (Skyline_Account_List_Q3.csv). Could you confirm who at Redwood should own the account mapping work? Happy to set a 30-minute sync.

Best,
Priya Rao
Head of Partnerships | Skyline Systems
priya.rao@skyline-systems.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Exploring Skyline Nexus + Redwood: co-sell mapping & integration

Forwarding Priya's list — primary ask is overlap + a practical stewardship model. Quick notes from me after a skim of the CSV:
- ~120 Skyline accounts in the data slice, mix of named enterprise and mid-market.
- A handful are already engaged with consulting partners (Nimbus, Altus) — we need to preserve those relationships.

Proposed guardrails (brainstorm):
- Tier-based ownership: named enterprise (>$500k ARR potential) => AE-led + partner co-sell; mid-market => partner-led with Redwood enablement.
- Product-fit carveouts: if Skyline is already deeply integrated (custom connectors), propose co-managed accounts.
- Routing rule: if AE has active opp within last 6 months, AE retains stewardship; otherwise apply partner routing.

Attaching an internal claims matrix for mapping (internal_claims_matrix.xlsx). Can you both review and flag accounts where Nimbus is already primary? Jonas — Karthik — any immediate redlines?

Best,
Marissa
Attachment: internal_claims_matrix.xlsx (Excel)

>

>
> Karthik, my ask: can we automate route decisions for inbound leads so partner-sourced leads get triaged into partner queues and AE-sourced leads into AE queues? That reduces friction.
>

I can extend one additional rule: if an account is in Skyline's B2B installed-base list and AE engagement is null, assign to Skyline partner lead queue and create a stewardship ticket in the CS system.

Subject: Skyline Nexus co-sell mesh and account routing proposal — MAP v1

Hi Priya / Sam — thanks for your patience while we evaluated the slice. Attached is our proposed MAP and the routing export (account-routing.csv). Highlights:

Summary of decisions
- 28 accounts marked as "consulting-partner-led" (Nimbus) — shared stewardship with scheduled weekly coordination windows.
- 42 accounts classified as "named enterprise": AE-led with Skyline co-sell privileges.
- remaining mid-market accounts routed to Skyline partner queue with enablement packets and a 2-week nurture cadence.

Mutual Action Plan (45 days)
1) Week 0: Sign off on MAP (this email). Please reply with a single-line affirmative if accepted.
2) Week 1: Execute routing import to Redwood's routing engine (Karthik to run).
3) Week 2–3: Joint outreach kit + enablement call for Skyline reps and Nimbus engineers.
4) Week 4–6: Run 2 pilot POCs (named accounts) and collect latency/cost delta metrics.
5) Week 7: Joint review and decision to expand or iterate.

Operational links & items
